column1: # How Kokoro should say words it gets wrong. narrate.py applies these to the text sent to the voice only: the script,
# the captions and the judged words keep the written form. One rule a line: a Python regex, a tab, what to say instead,
# a tab, why. Check a respelling with Kokoro's own phonemizer before adding it:
# A word only some uses of need, like the variable a (the article a is spoken right), gets a {say Eh} cue in the script.

column3: the book's lg is said "log"; Kokoro spells it "el-jee"
a capital A inside a sentence is a letter (array A, computer A): Kokoro says the article "uh"; "Eh" is /eɪ/
a sentence that opens "A of", "A is", … is about the letter A, not the article
von Neumann is "NOY-man" (Wikipedia: /vɒn ˈnɔɪmən/); Kokoro says "NEW-man"
Dijkstra is "DIKE-struh" in English (Dutch [ˈdɛikstra]); Kokoro says "DAYK-struh"
Michael Rabin, Hebrew רַבִּין, is "rah-BEEN"; Kokoro says "RAB-in"
the Rust compiler is "rust-see"; Kokoro says "rustk" (phonemized ɹˈʌstk)
